b: O my Lord, bless and grant peace always and forever
Upon Your beloved one, the Best of all Creation
Is it the memory of neighbours in Dhu Salam

f: مَزَجْتَ دَمْعًا جَرَى مِنْ مُقْلَةٍ بِدَمِ
b: That has left your eyes so red with tears?

f: أَمْ هَبَّتِ الرِّيحُ مِنْ تِلْقَاءِ كَاظِمَةٍ
b: Or is it the wind blowing from the direction of Kāẓima

f: وَأَوْمَضَ البَرْقُ فِي الظَّلْمَاءِ مِنْ إِضَمِ
b: And the lightning flashing in the black night from Mount Iḍam?

f: فَمَا لِعَيْنَيْكَ إِنْ قُلْتَ اكْفُفَا هَمَتَا
b: What is the matter with your eyes, that when you tell them to refrain,

f: وَمَا لِقَلْبِكَ إِنْ قُلْتَ اسْتَفِقْ يَهِمِ
b: They only weep more? And your heart – when you try to rouse it, It only becomes more bewildered
Does the one in love suppose his love can be concealed
Between pouring tears and a blazing heart?

f: لَوْلاَ الهَوَى لَمْ تُرِقْ دَمْعًا عَلَى طَلَلٍ
b: If not for love, your tears would not pour forth over traces left by your beloved,
Nor would you be sleepless remembering the willow tree and the mountain
So how can you deny this love when such honest witnesses
as weeping and looking gaunt have testified to it against you?
The agony of love has inscribed two lines of tears and grief
Upon your cheeks, pale as bahār4 and red as canam

f: نَعَمْ سَرَى طَيْفُ مَنْ أَهْوَى فَأَرَّقَنِي
b: Yes, a vision of the one I love came to me by night, and I could not sleep,
Oh, how love hinders the tasting of delight with its suffering!

f: يَا لَائِمِي فِي الهَوَى العُذْرِيِّ مَعْذِرَةً
b: O you who would rebuke me for this pure love, accept my excuse.

f: مِنِّي إِلَيْكَ وَلَوْ أَنْصَفْتَ لَمْ تَلُمِ
b: If you were truly fair, you would not reproach me at all
May you be spared a state such as mine! My secret cannot be concealed
From my detractors, nor will there ever be an end to my malady
You gave me sincere good counsel, but I did not hear it,

f: إِنَّ المُحِبَّ عَنِ العُذَّالِ فِي صَمَمِ
b: The lover is quite deaf to those who blame him

f: إِنِّي اتَّهَمْتُ نَصِيحَ الشَّيْبِ فِي عَذَلِي
b: I even suspected the counsel of my own grey hairs rebuking me,

f: وَالشَّيْبُ أَبْعَدُ فِي نُصْحٍ عَنِ التُّهَمِ
b: When I knew the counsel of old age and grey hair to be above suspicion
My foolish reckless self refused to heed the warning
Heralded by the onset of grey hair and old age

f: وَلاَ أَعَدَّتْ مِنَ الفِعْلِ الجَمِيلِ قِرَى
b: And it had not prepared any good deeds to properly welcome
This guest who had turned up on my head unannounced

f: لَوْ كُنْتُ أَعْلَمُ أَنِّي مَا أُوَقِّرُهُ
b: If I had known that I could not receive him with honour,
I would have hidden my secret from him with dye

f: مَنْ لِي بِرَدِّ جِمَاحٍ مِنْ غَوَايَتِهَا
b: Who can hold back my headstrong soul from the error of its ways,
Just as wild horses are restrained with bridles and reins?
Do not aim to break the desires by plunging further into sin,
The glutton’s greed is only increased by [the sight of] food

f: وَالنَّفْسُ كَالطِّفْلِ إِنْ تُهْمِلْهُ شَبَّ عَلَى
b: The self is like an infant, if you neglect its proper care, It will grow up still loving to suckle;
But once you wean it, it will be weaned
So dismiss its passions, beware of letting them take over, For when passion gets the upper hand,

f: إِنَّ الهَوَى مَا تَوَلَّى يُصْمِ أَوْ يَصِمِ
b: It will either kill or bring dishonour
Keep a watchful eye on it as it grazes in the field of actions,

f: وَإِنْ هِيَ اسْتَحْلَتِ المَرْعَى فَلاَ تُسِمِ
b: And if it finds the pasture too delightful, do not let it graze unchecked
How often a pleasure that is in fact deadly has seemed good,

f: مِنْ حَيْثُ لَمْ يَدْرِ أَنَّ السُّمَّ فِي الدَّسَمِ
b: To one who does not know there may be poison in the fat

f: وَاخْشَ الدَّسَائِسَ مِنْ جُوعٍ وَمِنْ شِبَعٍ
b: Beware the snares of hunger and satiety,
For an empty stomach may be worse than over-eating

f: وَاسْتَفْرِغِ الدَّمْعَ مِنْ عَيْنٍ قَدِ امْتَلَأَتْ
b: Dry the tears from eyes that have had their fill of forbidden things,
And henceforth let your only diet be regret
Oppose the self and shaytan – and defy them,
If they try to offer you advice, treat it with suspicion

f: وَلاَ تُطِعْ مِنْهُمَا خَصْمًا وَلاَ حَكَمًا
b: Never obey them, whether they oppose or come to arbitrate,
For you know by now the tricks of both opponents and arbitrators

f: أَسْتَغْفِرُ اللهَ مِنْ قَوْلٍ بِلاَ عَمَلٍ
b: I beg Allah’s forgiveness for saying things I do not do,

f: لَقَدْ نَسَبْتُ بِهِ نَسْلاً لِذِي عُقُمِ
b: As though I were ascribing progeny to one who was barren

f: أَمَرْتُكَ الخَيْرَ لَكِنْ مَا ائْتَمَرْتُ بِهِ
b: I ordered you to be good, but then didn’t heed my own advice,

f: وَمَا اسْتَقَمْتُ فَمَا قَوْلِي لَكَ اسْتَقِمِ
b: I was not myself upright, so what of my telling you, ‘Be upright!’
I have not made much provision of voluntary prayer Before death comes to take me,

f: وَلَمْ أُصَلِّ سِوَى فَرْضٍ وَلَمْ أَصُمِ
b: Neither have I prayed nor fasted more than was obligatory

f: ظَلَمْتُ سُنَّةَ مَنْ أَحْيَا الظَّلاَمَ إِلَى
b: I have done injustice to the path of the one who prayed at night

f: أَنِ اشْتَكَتْ قَدَمَاهُ الضُّرَّ مِنْ وَرَمِ
b: Until his feet complained of pain and swelling
While he bound up his insides against the extremity of his hunger,
Hiding his delicate skin beneath the stone tied round his waist
The high mountains of gold sought to entice him,
But he showed them in return the true meaning of elevation
His situation of austerity and need only confirmed His indifference to worldly concerns,

f: إِنَّ الضَّرُورَةَ لاَ تَعْدُو عَلَى العِصَمِ
b: For even dire need cannot assail such impeccable virtue

f: وَكَيْفَ تَدْعُو إِلَى الدُّنْيَا ضَرُورَةُ مَنْ
b: How could the dire need of such a person draw him towards the world,

f: لَوْلاَهُ لَمْ تُخْرَجِ الدُّنْيَا مِنَ العَدَمِ
b: When were it not for him, the world would never have emerged From non-existence?
Muhammad is the master of the two worlds, master of the jinn and men,

f: ـنِ وَالفَرِيقَيْنِ مِنْ عُرْبٍ وَمِنْ عَجَمِ
b: And master of the two groups, Arabs and non-Arabs
Our Prophet, who commands the good and forbids the wrong,

f: أَبَرَّ فِي قَوْلِ لاَ مِنْهُ وَلاَ نَعَمِ
b: There is no one truer to his word, whether it be ‘yes’ or ‘no’
He is the beloved one, whose intercession is hoped for
Against all the terrifying things that take us by storm
He has called people to Allah, so those who cling to him
Are clinging to a rope which will never break

f: فَاقَ النَبِيِّينَ فِي خَلْقٍ وَفِي خُلُقٍ
b: He surpassed the other prophets both in form and noble character,

f: وَلَمْ يُدَانُوهُ فِي عِلْمٍ وَلاَ كَرَمِ
b: And none has come close to him in knowledge or in pure generosity
They all petition the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for just a handful of water

f: غَرْفًا مِنَ البَحْرِ أَوْ رَشْفًا مِنَ الدِّيَمِ
b: From his ocean, or a draught from his never-ending rain
They all come to a halt before him according to their measure,

f: مِنْ نُقْطَةِ العِلْمِ أَوْ مِنْ شَكْلَةِ الحِكَمِ
b: As diacritical points upon his knowledge, or vowel marks upon his wisdom
He is the one in whom meaning and form were perfected,
And then the One who created all mankind Chose him as His beloved
He is far from having any equal in his virtues,
For in him, the essence of perfection is indivisible

f: دَعْ مَا ادَّعَتْهُ النَّصَارَى فِي نَبِيِّهِمِ
b: Abandon what the Christians have claimed about their Prophet,

f: وَاحْكُمْ بِمَا شِئْتَ مَدْحًا فِيهِ وَاحْتَكِمِ
b: Beyond that you may say whatever you wish in praise of him

f: وَانْسُبْ إِلَى ذَاتِهِ مَا شِئْتَ مِنْ شَرَفٍ
b: You may ascribe whatever you wish of nobility to his essence,

f: وَانْسُبْ إِلَى قَدْرِهِ مَا شِئْتَ مِنْ عِظَمِ
b: And to his rank, whatever you wish of greatness

f: فَإِنَّ فَضْلَ رَسُولِ اللهِ لَيْسَ لَهُ
b: Indeed, the high merit of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ has no furthest limit
Which could be expressed by the tongue of a human being
Were his miracles to be as mighty as his rank,

f: أَحْيَا اسْمُهُ حِينَ يُدْعَى دَارِسَ الرِّمَمِ
b: Just the sound of his name would bring dead bones to life

f: لَمْ يَمْتَحِنَّا بِمَا تَعْيَا العُقُولُ بِهِ
b: He did not test us with things that would exhaust our intellects,

f: حِرْصًا عَلَيْنَا فَلَمْ نَرْتَبْ وَلَمْ نَهِمِ
b: Out of concern for us, so we did not fall into doubt or bewilderment

f: أَعْيَا الوَرَى فَهْمُ مَعْنَاهُ فَلَيْسَ يُرَى
b: Mankind is unable to comprehend his true essence,

f: فِي القُرْبِ وَالبُعْدِ فِيهِ غَيْرُ مُنْفَحِمِ
b: Near and far, they are dumbfounded
Like the sun, which from afar appears small to the naked eye,
Whereas up close, it would dim and dazzle the vision
How can people who are asleep perceive his true reality
In this world, while they are distracted from him by their dreams?
The extent of the knowledge we have of him is that he is a man,
And that he is the best of all Allah’s creation

f: وَكُلُّ آيٍ أَتَى الرُّسْلُ الكِرَامُ بِهَا
b: Every miracle brought by the Noble Messengers
Was only connected to them through his light
Surely he is a sun of bounty and they are its planets,
Manifesting their lights for people in the darkness
How generous the creation of a Prophet Adorned with excellent character!
So graced with beauty, and radiant of face

f: كَالزَّهْرِ فِي تَرَفٍ وَالبَدْرِ فِي شَرَفٍ
b: Like a flower in freshness and a full moon in eminence,

f: وَالبَحْرِ فِي كَرَمٍ وَالدَّهْرِ فِي هِمَمِ
b: Like an ocean in pure generosity and like Time itself In strength of resolution
Just from his majestic bearing, even when he was alone,

f: فِي عَسْكَرٍ حِينَ تَلْقَاهُ وَفِي حَشَمِ
b: He seemed as if amongst a great army and entourage
It was as if shining pearls, protected in their shells,
Emerged from both his speech and his radiant smile

f: لاَ طِيبَ يَعْدِلُ تُرْبًا ضَمَّ أَعْظُمَهُ
b: No perfume could ever match that of the earth that holds his noble form,
What bliss for the one who smells that blessed earth or kisses it!
His birth made clear the purity of his origin,
O how pure his beginning and his end!
On that day, the Persians realized they had been warned
Of the onset of misery and disasters
That very night a crack appeared in the Arch of Chosroes,
Just as the unity and cohesion of his people was forever lost
The fire, out of grief for the loss, breathed its last,

f: عَلَيْهِ وَالنَّهْرُ سَاهِي العَيْنِ مِنْ سَدَمِ
b: And the river was distracted from its course by sorrow
Sawa was troubled as the waters of its lake receded,
And the one who came to drink from it returned raging with thirst

f: كَأَنَّ بِالنَّارِ مَا بِالمَاءِ مِنْ بَلَلٍ
b: It was as though, from grief, the fire took on water’s wetness,

f: حُزْنًا وَبِالمَاءِ مَا بِالنَّارِ مِنْ ضَرَمِ
b: And water took on the blazing dryness of the fire
The jinn were shrieking, and the lights were flashing out,

f: وَالحَقُّ يَظْهَرُ مِنْ مَعْنىً وَمِنْ كَلِمِ
b: As the truth was made manifest in both meaning and word
But blind and deaf, the Persians did not hear the happy tidings,
Neither did they see the flash of warning signs

f: مِنْ بَعْدِ مَا أَخْبَرَ الأَقْوَامَ كَاهِنُهُمْ
b: Even after the people’s own soothsayers had told them
That their crooked old religion could not last

f: وَبَعْدَمَا عَايَنُوا فِي الأُفْقِ مِنْ شُهُبٍ
b: And after they had seen shooting stars away on the horizon,

f: مُنْقَضَّةٍ وَفْقَ مَا فِي الأَرْضِ مِنْ صَنَمِ
b: Falling from the heavens, just as the idols were falling on earth

f: حَتَّى غَدَا عَنْ طَرِيقِ الوَحْيِ مُنْهَزِمٌ
b: Until even the devils were routed, fleeing from the path of revelation,
Following after others as they fled
They were fleeing just like Abraha’s warriors,

f: أَوْ عَسْكَرٍ بِالحَصَى مِنْ رَاحَتَيْهِ رُمِي
b: Or like the army scattered by pebbles thrown From the Prophet’s ﷺ own hand
Thrown by him after glorifying God in the palm of his hand,
As the one who glorified his Lord was thrown out From the belly of the whale
Trees came to him when he called, prostrating,

f: تَمْشِي إِلَيْهِ عَلَى سَاقٍ بِلاَ قَدَمِ
b: Walking towards him on trunks that had no feet
As though they had written lines of beautiful calligraphy
With their branches all along the path
Like the cloud that moved with him wherever he went,
Protecting him from the fierce oven of the midday heat
I swear by the [Lord of the] moon that was split in two,
Surely it has a connection with his heart, A true and blessed oath

f: وَمَا حَوَى الغَارُ مِنْ خَيْرٍ وَمِنْ كَرَمِ
b: And by the excellence and nobility encompassed in the cave,

f: وَكُلُّ طَرْفٍ مِنَ الكُفَّارِ عَنْهُ عَمِي
b: While every glance of the unbelievers was quite blind to it

f: فَالصِّدْقُ فِي الغَارِ وَالصِّدِّيقُ لَمْ يَرِمَا
b: The true one and the truthful one remained in the cave,

f: وَهُمْ يَقُولُونَ مَا بِالغَارِ مِنْ أَرِمِ
b: As those outside said to one another, ‘There is no one in this cave.’
They did not suspect that a dove would hover giving protection,

f: خَيْرِ البَرِيَّةِ لَمْ تَنْسُجْ وَلَمْ تَحُمِ
b: Or that a spider would spin its web to help the Best of Creation
Allah’s solicitude and shelter freed him from the need to resort

f: مِنَ الدُّرُوعِ وَعَنْ عَالٍ مِنَ الأُطُمِ
b: To coats of armour and fortresses for his protection

f: مَا سَامَنِي الدَّهْرُ ضَيْمًا وَاسْتَجَرْتُ بِهِ
b: Whenever the times have treated me unjustly, and I have turned to him

f: إِلاَّ وَنِلْتُ جِوَارًا مِنْهُ لَمْ يُضَمِ
b: For refuge, I always found security with him, unharmed

f: وَلاَ الْتَمَسْتُ غِنَى الدَّارَيْنِ مِنْ يَدِهِ
b: And never have I sought the wealth of the two worlds from his hand,

f: إِلاَّ اسْتَلَمْتُ النَّدَى مِنْ خَيْرِ مُسْتَلَمِ
b: Without receiving open-handed generosity from the best of givers

f: لاَ تُنْكِرِ الوَحْيَ مِنْ رُؤْيَاهُ إِنَّ لَهُ
b: Do not deny the revelations he received in his dreams,

f: قَلْبًا إِذَا نَامَتِ العَيْنَانِ لَمْ يَنَمِ
b: For surely, though his eyes would sleep, he had a heart that never slept
That was from the time when he attained to prophethood,
For the dreams of the one who has come of age cannot be denied
God be praised! Revelation is not something acquired,
Nor is a prophet’s knowledge of the unseen to be suspected
How many sick people have been healed at the touch of his hand,
And how many, driven almost mad by the noose of their sins, Have been set free
His supplication brought new life in the year of barren dryness,

f: حَتَّى حَكَتْ غُرَّةً فِي الأَعْصُرِ الدُّهُمِ
b: So that it stood out among the dark years Like the beautiful white blaze on a horse’s forehead

f: بِعَارضٍ جَادَ أَوْ خِلْتَ البِطَاحَ بِهَا
b: The clouds poured down rain, until you would have thought

f: سَيْبًا مِنَ اليَمِّ أَوْ سَيْلاً مِنَ العَرِمِ
b: The valley was flowing with water from the open sea, Or from the burst dam of ‘Arim
Allow me to describe to you the signs that appeared to him,

f: ظُهُورَ نَارِ القِرَى لَيْلاً عَلَى عَلَمِ
b: Clearly visible like beacons lit at night On the high hills to welcome guests
Although a pearl’s beauty is increased when strung among others,
Its value is not lessened when alone, unstrung
What hope can the one who tries to praise it have

f: مَا فِيهِ مِنْ كَرَمِ الأَخْلاَقِ وَالشِّيَمِ
b: Of doing justice to its noble traits and qualities?
Verses of truth from the Merciful — revealed in time,
Yet Eternal — the attribute of the Pre-eternal One
They are not bound by time, and bring us tidings

f: عَنِ المَعَادِ وَعَنْ عَادٍ وَعَنْ إِرَمِ
b: Of the Last Day, and also of ‘Ad and Iram
They have lasted to our time, and outstripped

f: مِنَ النَّبِيِّينَ إِذْ جَاءَتْ وَلَمْ تَدُمِ
b: Every miracle brought by other prophets, Which came, but did not last
Verses so clear that no obscurity can remain

f: لِذِي شِقَاقٍ وَمَا تَبْغِينَ مِنْ حَكَمِ
b: For the wrangler, nor do they require any judge

f: مَا حُورِبَتْ قَطُّ إِلاَّ عَادَ مِنْ حَرَبٍ
b: No implacable enemy has ever attacked them
Without retreating at last from the battle, begging for peace
Their very eloquence refutes the claim of one opposing them,

f: رَدَّ الغَيُورِ يَدَ الجَانِي عَنِ الحُرَمِ
b: As an honourable man wards off the assailant’s hand From what is sacred

f: لَهَا مَعَانٍ كَمَوْجِ البَحْرِ فِي مَدَدٍ
b: They contain meanings like the sea’s never-ending waves,
And go far beyond its jewels in their beauty and value
Their wonders are numberless and incalculable,
Nor does their constant repetition ever result in weariness or boredom

f: قَرَّتْ بِهَا عَيْنُ قَارِيهَا فَقُلْتُ لَهُ
b: The one who recited them was filled with delight, and I said to him,
“Truly you have seized the rope of Allah — so hold on to it.”

f: إِنْ تَتْلُهَا خِيفَةً مِنْ حَرِّ نَارِ لَظَى
b: If you recite them fearing the heat of the blazing Fire,

f: أَطْفَأْتَ حَرَّ لَظَى مِنْ وِرْدِهَا الشَّبِمِ
b: You have extinguished the heat of the blaze by their cool sweet water
Like the Ḥawḍ, which makes bright the faces of the disobedient,
When they had arrived with faces black as coal
Like the Ṣirāṭ and like the Balance Scales in justice,

f: فَالقِسْطُ مِنْ غَيْرِهَا فِي النَّاسِ لَمْ يَقُمِ
b: True justice among men cannot be established from any other
Do not be surprised if an envious person refuses to acknowledge them,
Affecting ignorance, even though perfectly able to understand

f: قَدْ تُنْكِرُ العَيْنُ ضَوْءَ الشَّمْسِ مِنْ رَمَدٍ
b: For the eye may reject the sun’s light when it is inflamed,

f: وَيُنْكِرُ الفَمُ طَعْمَ المَاءِ مِنْ سَقَمِ
b: And when the body is unwell, The mouth may shun even the taste of sweet water

f: يَا خَيْرَ مَنْ يَمَّمَ العَافُونَ سَاحَتَهُ
b: O best of those to whose courtyards repair the seekers of blessings,
On foot and on the backs of laden camels
O you who are the greatest sign for the one able to perceive,
And the most sublime blessing for the one desiring benefit

f: سَرَيْتَ مِنْ حَرَمٍ لَيْلاً إِلَى حَرَمٍ
b: You travelled by night from one sacred place to yet another,

f: كَمَا سَرَى البَدْرُ فِي دَاجٍ مِنَ الظُّلَمِ
b: Just as the full moon travels across the pitch-black sky

f: وَبِتَّ تَرْقَى إِلَى أَنْ نِلْتَ مَنْزِلَةً
b: That night you ascended until you reached a station of nearness,

f: مِنْ قَابِ قَوْسَيْنِ لَمْ تُدْرَكْ وَلَمْ تُرَمِ
b: Only two bows-lengths distant, A station never before attained or even hoped for
Thus all the Prophets and Messengers gave precedence to you,
The precedence of a master over those who serve him
You traversed the Seven Heavens with them,

f: فِي مَوْكِبٍ كُنْتَ فِيهِ صَاحِبَ العَلَمِ
b: And you were the standard bearer – leading their procession

f: حَتَّى إِذَا لَمْ تَدَعْ شَأْوًا لِمُسْتَبِقٍ
b: Until you left no greater goal for the seeker of eminence and proximity,
Nor any higher station for the one seeking elevation
All other stations seemed lower in comparison with yours,
Since you were proclaimed in the highest terms – the unique one
So that you would achieve a station of perfect proximity,
Hidden from the eyes, And obtain a secret concealed from all creation
So you attained to every excellence without equal,
And you passed alone through every station, far from all others

f: وَجَلَّ مِقْدَارُ مَا وُلِّيتَ مِنْ رُتَبٍ
b: Sublime indeed is the measure of the ranks you have been granted,

f: وَعَزَّ إِدْرَاكُ مَا أُولِيتَ مِنْ نِعَمِ
b: Beyond comprehension the blessings bestowed upon you

f: بُشْرَى لَنَا مَعْشَرَ الإِسْلَامِ إِنَّ لَنَا
b: Glad tidings for us, O assembly of Muslims,
For truly we have a pillar of support and solicitude That can never be destroyed
When God named the one who called us to obey Him,
The noblest of Messengers, Henceforward we became the noblest of peoples
News of his marching out cast fear into the hearts of the enemy,
Just as heedless goats are startled at a sudden noise

f: مَا زَالَ يَلْقَاهُمُ فِي كُلِّ مُعْتَرَكٍ
b: He continued to meet them on every battleground,

f: حَتَّى حَكَوْا بِالقَنَا لَحْمًا عَلَى وَضَمِ
b: Until they were cut to pieces by spears, Like meat upon a butcher’s block
They were longing to flee, almost envying
The corpses carried off by the eagles and vultures
The nights passed, without them being able to keep count,

f: مَا لَمْ تَكُنْ مِنْ لَيَالِي الأَشْهُرِ الحُرُمِ
b: Except if they were the nights of the Sacred Months
As if the religion were a guest that had arrived at their courtyards,

f: بِكُلِّ قَرْمٍ إِلَى لَحْمِ العِدَا قَرِمِ
b: With every brave chieftain ready to rend the flesh of their enemies
Bringing in its wake a sea of armed men upon fast horses,
Hurling forth waves of brave warriors in clashing tumult
Each responding to Allah’s summons, seeking His good pleasure,
Mounting a fierce assault, to tear out unbelief by its roots

f: حَتىَّ غَدَتْ مِلَّةُ الإِسْلاَمِ وَهْيَ بِهِمْ
b: Until the religion of Islam, thanks to them,
After banishment from her homeland, Was once again united with her kin
Ever protected from her enemies by the best father

f: وَخَيْرِ بَعْلٍ فَلَمْ تَيْتَمْ وَلَمْ تَئِمِ
b: And most excellent husband, So that she was neither orphaned nor widowed
They were mountains — ask those who fought against them,

f: مَاذَا رَأَى مِنْهُمُ فِي كُلِّ مُصْطَدَمِ
b: Just what they saw of them on every battlefield

f: وَسَلْ حُنَيْنًا وَسَلْ بَدْرًا وَسَلْ أُحُدًا
b: Ask Hunayn, ask Badr, ask Uhud — seasons of death and destruction,

f: فُصُولَ حَتْفٍ لَهُمْ أَدْهَى مِنَ الوَخَمِ
b: More calamitous for them than fatal epidemics

f: المُصْدِرِي البِيضِ حُمْرًا بَعْدَ مَا وَرَدَتْ
b: Their burnished swords returned quenched and bloody,

f: مِنَ العِدَا كُلَّ مُسْوَدٍّ مِنَ اللِّمَمِ
b: After drinking deep beneath black locks on their enemies’ heads
Like writers wielding reed pens for spears,
Their pens left no part of the bodies unpointed or unmarked
Bristling with arms, yet a special quality distinguished them,
Just as a rose differs by its fragrance From the thorny salam tree
The winds of victory would present to you their fragrance,

f: فَتَحْسَبُ الزَّهْرَ فِي الأَكْمَامِ كُلَّ كَمِي
b: So that you imagine each valiant one of them To be a beautiful flower in bud

f: كَأَنَّهُمْ فِي ظُهُورِ الخَيْلِ نَبْتُ رُبًا
b: As if, riding their steeds, they were flowers blooming upon a height,

f: مِنْ شِدَّةِ الحَزْمِ لاَ مِنْ شَدَّةِ الحُزُمِ
b: Held there not by the tautness of their saddles, But by the firmness of their resolve

f: طَارَتْ قُلُوبُ العِدَا مِنْ بَأْسِهِمْ فَرَقًا
b: The enemy hearts in turmoil, terrified at their mighty power,
Could hardly tell brave warriors from herds of sheep
Those whose help comes from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ —

f: إِنْ تَلْقَهُ الأُسْدُ فِي آجَامِهَا تَجِمِ
b: Even lions encountering them in their dens would be struck dumb with fear

f: وَلَنْ تَرَى مِنْ وَليٍّ غَيْرِ مُنْتَصِرٍ
b: You would never see a friend of his unaided by him,

f: بِهِ وَلاَ مِنْ عَدُوٍّ غَيْرِ مُنْقَصِمِ
b: Nor yet an enemy of his undefeated
He established his community within the fortress of his religion,

f: كَاللَّيْثِ حَلَّ مَعَ الأَشْبَالِ فِي أَجَمِ
b: As the lion settles down with its cubs in its lair

f: كَمْ جَدَّلَتْ كَلِمَاتُ اللهِ مِنْ جَدِلٍ
b: How often have the words of Allah

f: فِيهِ وَكَمْ خَصَمَ البُرْهَانُ مِنْ خَصِمِ
b: Thrown down those who contended with him! How often has the Clear Proof defeated his opponents in argument!
Enough of a miracle for you — such knowledge found
In someone unlettered, living in the Age of Ignorance, And such refinement in an orphan!
I have served him with my praise, seeking pardon

f: ذُنُوبَ عُمْرٍ مَضَى فِي الشِّعْرِ وَالخِدَمِ
b: For the sins of a life spent in poetry and the service of others
Garlanded with these two sins, the consequences of which I dread
It is as though I were now a sacrificial animal

f: أَطَعْتُ غَيَّ الصِّبَا فِي الحَالَتَيْنِ وَمَا
b: In both these errors I followed only the reckless delinquency of youth
Achieving nothing in the end but wrong action and regret
Alas for a soul that has met with only loss in its transactions!

f: لَمْ تَشْتَرِ الدِّينَ بِالدُّنْيَا وَلَمْ تَسُمِ
b: It did not use this world to help secure the Next, Nor even to embark upon negotiations
Whoever sells his Hereafter in exchange for this world,

f: يَبِنْ لَهُ الغَبْنُ فِي بَيْعٍ وَفِي سَلَمِ
b: Soon discovers he has been cheated, both in present and future gains

f: إِنْ آتِ ذَنْبًا فَمَا عَهْدِي بِمُنْتَقِضٍ
b: If I were to commit a sin, it would not break
My contract with the Prophet ﷺ, Nor cut off my connection to him
For I have a covenant of protection from him
By my being named Muhammad, and he is the most faithful Of all mankind in keeping trusts

f: إِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ فِي مَعَادِي آخِذًا بِيَدِي
b: On the Day of Rising, if he does not take me by the hand

f: فَضْلاً وَإِلاَّ فَقُلْ يَا زَلَّةَ القَدَمِ
b: Out of pure kindness, then just say, “What a terrible end!”
Far be it from him to ever deprive the hopeful one Of his generous gifts,

f: أَوْ يَرْجِعَ الجَارُ مِنْهُ غَيْرَ مُحْتَرَمِ
b: Or to turn back someone seeking refuge Without treating him honourably
For ever since I have devoted all my thoughts to his praise,
I have found him to be the best guarantor of my salvation

f: وَلَنْ يَفُوتَ الغِنَى مِنْهُ يَدًا تَرِبَتْ
b: His bounty will not fail even a hand that is dusty and poor,

f: إِنَّ الحَيَا يُنْبِتَ الأَزْهَارَ فِي الأَكَمِ
b: For surely the rain may bring forth flowers even on the rockiest of slopes

f: وَلَمْ أُرِدْ زَهْرَةَ الدُّنْيَا الَّتِي اقْتَطَفَتْ
b: Indeed, I have no more desire for the flowers of this world,

f: يَدَا زُهَيْرٍ بِمَا أَثْنَى عَلَى هَرِمِ
b: Like those gathered in by the hands of Zuhayr For his praise of Ḥarim

f: يَا أَكْرَمَ الخَلْقِ مَالِي مَنْ أَلُوذُ بِهِ
b: O most Noble of all Creation, whose protection can I seek
But yours, when the Great Catastrophe overtakes us?

f: وَلَنْ يَضِيقَ رَسُولَ اللهِ جَاهُكَ بِي
b: O Messenger of Allah ﷺ, your great rank Will not be lessened by my petition,
If the Generous One appears as the Avenger
For surely this world and its companion the Next Are from your generosity.
And part of your knowledge Is knowledge of the Preserved Tablet and of the Pen

f: يَا نَفْسُ لاَ تَقْنَطِي مِنْ زَلَّةٍ عَظُمَتْ
b: O my soul, do not despair over an error which may appear immense,
For surely even grave sins, with divine forgiveness, Are more like minor lapses
It may be that my Lord’s mercy, when He distributes it,

f: تَأْتِي عَلَى حَسَبِ العِصْيَانِ فِي القِسَمِ
b: Will be apportioned in accordance with the magnitude of sins

f: يَا رَبِّ وَاجْعَلْ رَجَائِي غَيْرَ مُنْعَكِسٍ
b: O my Lord, let not my hopes in You be cast back unfulfilled,
Nor let my firm conviction of Your goodness be thrown into disarray

f: وَالْطُفْ بِعَبْدِكَ فِي الدَّارَيْنِ إِنَّ لَهُ
b: Be kind to Your servant, both in this world and the Next,
For his patience, when called upon by dreadful fears, just disappears
And let a cloud of blessings from You pour down
Upon the Prophet ﷺ, raining down unceasingly

f: مَا رَنَّحَتْ عَذَبَاتِ البَانِ رِيحُ صَبًا
b: As long as the easterly breezes sway the willow boughs,
And the caravan leader urges on his white camels, Delighting them with his songs

f: ثُمَّ الرِّضَا عَنْ أَبِي بَكْرٍ وَعَنْ عُمَرٍ
b: And grant Your good pleasure to Abu Bakr and ʿUmar رضي الله عنهما,

f: وَعَنْ عَلِيٍّ وَعَنْ عُثْمَانَ ذِي الكَرَمِ
b: And to ʿAli رضي الله عنه and ʿUthman رضي الله عنه, the noble and generous
And to the Family and the Companions and Followers,
For they are the people of true mindfulness of God, And of purity, forbearance, and generosity
O my Lord, by the Chosen One, let us attain all that we are hoping for,

f: وَاغْفِرْ لَنَا مَا مَضَى يَا وَاسِعَ الكَرَمِ
b: And pardon us for what has passed, O Boundlessly Generous One
And, O God, forgive all the Muslims their wrong actions,

f: يَتْلُونَ فِي المَسْجِدِ الأَقْصَى وَفِي الحَرَمِ
b: By that which they recite in the Masjid al-Aqsa, As well as in the Ancient Sanctuary

f: بِجَاهِ مَنْ بَيْتُهُ فِي طَيْبَةٍ حَرَمٌ
b: By the rank of the one whose dwelling is a sanctuary in Tayba,
And whose very name is one of the greatest of oaths
This Burda of the Chosen One is now complete,

f: وَالحَمْدُ لِلّهِ فِي بَدْءٍ وَفِي خَتَمِ
b: Praise be to Allah for its beginning and for its end

f: أَبْيَاتُهَا قَدْ أَتَتْ سِتِّينَ مَعْ مِائَةٍ
b: Its verses number one hundred and sixty,

f: فَرِّجْ بِهَا كَرْبَنَا يَا وَاسِعَ الكَرَمِ
b: Ease, by them, all of our difficulties, O Boundlessly Generous Lord
